intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene on chromosome X.

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: The TBX22 gene is located on chromosome X.
checks.evidence_quote: X-linked cleft palate (CPX) is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the TBX22 transcription factor
checks.explanation: X-linked disorder caused by TBX22 implies an X-chromosome location; standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977). Pauws et al. (2013) described it as an X-linked, CHARGE-like syndrome, and its sensorineural deafness and coloboma extend the phenotype beyond that seen in classic X-linked cleft palate, which is also caused by TBX22 mutation.

checks.explanation: Cleft palate is listed as a feature of the syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) noted that the family they first reported (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977) had been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome. On follow-up, they concluded that the patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome or association. Pauws et al. (2013) called the disorder X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) noted that the family first reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) had been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: This family has been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the authors' previously reported family had been cited as familial CHARGE syndrome. It calls this their earlier report but does not give its year (1977).

checks.claim: On follow-up, Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) concluded that the patients in the family first reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) did not have familial CHARGE syndrome or association.
checks.evidence_quote: We do not think that the patients in this family have the Charge syndrome or association.
checks.explanation: The authors reject both CHARGE syndrome and CHARGE association, and after the follow-up study they conclude the patients do not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) carried out a follow-up study of the family reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) to assess how the patients had developed since and whether they had CHARGE syndrome. They concluded that the patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

checks.evidence_quote: we decided to do a follow-up study on this family to assess the subsequent development of the patients and to determine if they have the CHARGE syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states both aims of the follow-up study directly.

checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that our patients do not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Pauws et al. (2013) noted that the phenotype in the family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome included sensorineural deafness and coloboma. These features are suggested by the developmental expression pattern of Tbx22 but had not previously been associated with X-linked cleft palate.

paragraphs.text: Based on the family history, Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage. Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) later referred to the disorder as a new X-linked syndrome. Pauws et al. (2013) found a TBX22 mutation that tracked with the phenotype in the original family, which supports X-linked inheritance.

checks.claim: Based on the family history, Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage for the syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.

checks.evidence_quote: Re-evaluation of new X-linked syndrome for evidence of CHARGE syndrome or association.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) found a TBX22 mutation that tracked with the phenotype in the original Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome family.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
checks.explanation: The mutation tracking with the phenotype is stated, but the abstract does not say this is the family originally reported by Abruzzo and Erickson.

checks.claim: Segregation of a TBX22 mutation with the phenotype in the original Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome family supports X-linked inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: This study hypothesized a possible involvement of TBX22 in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome
checks.explanation: The family is described as X-linked, but the abstract does not explicitly say that segregation supports X-linked inheritance.

paragraphs.text: In a family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, Pauws et al. (2013) identified a novel splice acceptor mutation in the TBX22 gene (c.593-5T-A) that tracked with the phenotype. They also identified a novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G-A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G-A) in patients with classic X-linked cleft palate. Both affected the same exon. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that all 3 variants would abolish normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro assay suggested that alternative splice sites were likely to be used instead. Pauws et al. (2013) concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, which expands the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) identified a novel splice acceptor mutation in the TBX22 gene, c.593-5T-A, in a family with Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
checks.explanation: The abstract names the family as having X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

checks.claim: In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that the TBX22 variants c.593-5T-A, c.767+5G-A, and c.767+1G-A would each abolish normal mRNA splicing.

checks.explanation: Abstract says all three variants were predicted to abolish normal splicing, in the context of the in silico and in vitro analyses.

checks.evidence_quote: an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome
